pr.title: docs(second-brain): add machine contracts for ADR acceptance evidence
pr.body:
Closes the architecture-time machine-contract evidence gap blocking amended acceptance condition #2 for ADR-SB-001..010.

Before this change nothing in the repository could satisfy "machine contracts required by this ADR MUST parse and cover the decision at ADR acceptance": every ADR-named type (LocalSpoolPort, CustodyPort, OpenLoopCandidate, TaskProposal, TaskPromotionRequest, project identity envelope, service capability receipt) existed only as prose. That gap is reproduced and recorded in BASELINE_CONTRACT_INVENTORY.json before any artifact was authored.

Adds a repository-owned contract family under schemas/second_brain/contracts/ — two meta-schemas, ten per-ADR contracts carrying 97 structured decision clauses, seven typed artifacts for the types the ADRs name directly, and a coverage matrix at 97/97 COVERED with MISSING=0 and AMBIGUOUS=0.

The coverage denominator is frozen in its own earlier commit, before any contract existed, so git history proves the freeze preceded authoring. Every clause binds verbatim fragments of the ratified candidate e4b28946..., machine-verified in both directions.

A fail-closed validator (113 checks) and an adversarial matrix (46 tests executing the real validator against mutated repository copies) prove the evidence cannot false-green. Semantic mutations are applied consistently across inventory and contract, so a mutation that keeps the right shape and changes the architecture decision is still rejected.

Also reconciles the stale fo-01-repair-status.json against its later independent-verification receipt; the two records on main disagreed about whether FO-01 still blocked ADR acceptance.

Accepts no ADR. All ten remain PROPOSED, the document remains CANDIDATE, SB-DEC-026 remains unlinked, and implementation execution remains NOT_AUTHORIZED. Denial fixtures remain an implementation-time gate and are explicitly not implemented.
